title: Youth mental health is being framed as a cross-system social and institutional condition, not only a clinical outcome
source_unit: United Nations DESA, World Youth Report: Youth Mental Health and Well-being
geography: Global youth well-being publication drawing on comparative literature, expert input, youth consultations, and lived-experience material

observations.period: 2025-2026; cross-sector framework for youth mental health and well-being

denominator.unit: global UN youth mental-health synthesis report

linked_social_determinants.unit: interlinked domains identified by the report: education, employment, family dynamics, poverty and deprivation, technology and digital environment, and society and community

cross_sectoral_approach.unit: policy orientation for addressing youth mental health and well-being

observations.method: UN DESA synthesis of literature review, expert consultation, youth consultation, lived-experience material, and cross-sector policy analysis.
observations.uncertainty: The report synthesizes mechanisms and policy evidence rather than estimating one global causal effect. The six domains interact differently across age, gender, culture, place, disability, conflict, and income contexts.
observations.subgroup: Young people across education, employment, family, poverty, technology, community, and service-access contexts.
observations.counterinterpretation: A social-determinants framework does not make clinical care unnecessary; it indicates that treatment capacity alone cannot address upstream exposure, stigma, exclusion, or institutional conditions.

denominator.unit: global comparative evidence synthesis on youth mental-health disparities

inequality_mechanism.value: unequal access to opportunities and resources plus differential exposure to risks
inequality_mechanism.unit: reported pathway linking social conditions to disparities in youth mental-health outcomes

stigma_barriers.value: stigma and discrimination can limit help-seeking, health-care access, education, and decent work
stigma_barriers.unit: reported institutional and social barrier pattern

observations.method: Comparative synthesis of social determinants, inequalities, stigma, discrimination, service access, and prevention evidence described in the report.
observations.uncertainty: The report does not identify a single universal ordering of causes or quantify the same pathway in every country; mental-health outcomes and service access remain context-sensitive and multidimensional.
observations.subgroup: Young people facing poverty, discrimination, stigma, conflict, climate disruption, insecure work, educational pressure, family stress, or unequal access to care and opportunity.
observations.counterinterpretation: Not every exposure produces poor mental health, and strong relationships, community support, agency, and accessible care can be protective; the report is not a deficit description of youth.

observations.period: 2025-2026; school, work, family, digital, and community institutions

denominator.unit: global youth mental-health policy and institutional-response frame

school_route.value: supportive school environments, social-emotional learning, and adequately funded mental-wellness programmes
school_route.unit: institutional response route identified by the report

work_transition_route.value: education-to-work transitions, job insecurity, workplace stress, and fair remuneration are relevant to youth well-being
work_transition_route.unit: institutional transition route identified by the report

digital_route.value: online environments can support education and connection while also creating risks such as cyberbullying and harmful dependence
digital_route.unit: technology and digital-environment trade-off identified by the report

youth_led_action.unit: role for youth-led initiatives in comprehensive mental-health responses

observations.method: UN DESA institutional synthesis connecting education, employment, family, technology, community, prevention, early intervention, privacy, and youth participation.
observations.uncertainty: The publication identifies actionable institutional routes but does not establish that a particular school, employer, platform, or youth-led programme produces a specified outcome without local evaluation.
observations.subgroup: Schools, employers, families, health and social services, digital platforms, community organizations, policymakers, and youth-led initiatives.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional support can improve opportunity and resilience without eliminating structural stress; privacy protection and youth agency are conditions of trustworthy data and intervention.

related_sources.claim: Official UN DESA full report and executive-summary material.
Official UN publication file with the report's cross-determinant synthesis.

boundary: This record adds a youth mental-health-to-social-determinants, institutional-access, prevention, digital-environment, education-to-work, and youth-agency route. It is not a respondent-level estimate, clinical prevalence series, diagnosis, treatment-effect study, or proof that any single determinant caused an individual outcome.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official UN DESA publication page, executive summary, full report, and youth-report information page were retrieved; the six-determinant framework, inequality and stigma mechanisms, institutional routes, prevention, privacy, and youth-led recommendations were cross-checked across official materials.
